title: scheduler-observability-contract-and-simulated-injector-2026
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview:

This document defines the Scheduler Observability Contract for Redwood's serving runtime and describes an accompanying Simulated Injector tool used to validate telemetry pipelines end-to-end. The goal is to make scheduler behavior (admission, batching, kernel mapping, preemption, and handoff) observable through a small, stable set of events and metrics so SRE, runtime, and profiling teams can reliably detect regressions, diagnose incidents, and run automated acceptance tests during rollouts.

Audience:
- Runtime engineers (owners of kernel/scheduler code)
- SRE and oncall teams
- Profiling and benchmarking teams
- Observability and telemetry platform owners

Contract principles (high level):
1) Minimalism: Emit a compact set of structured events that capture decisions and state transitions. Avoid duplicating high-volume token-level logs.
2) Deterministic schemas: Every event must follow a documented JSON schema with stable field names (snake_case). Changes require cross-team review.
3) Cost-aware sampling: High-frequency internal traces are sampled; key transition events must be unsampled or sampled with guaranteed floor rates for SLO monitoring.
4) End-to-end testability: A simulator must be able to inject synthetic traces that exercise normal and pathological scheduler flows; observability owners are responsible for ingest test harnesses.

Event taxonomy (summary):
- scheduler_decision: Admission decision for an incoming request (accept/reject/defer).
- batch_formation: When the scheduler assembles a batch (includes batch shape, kernel_hint).
- kernel_dispatch: When a kernel is selected and dispatched to an accelerator.
- preemption_event: When a running kernel is preempted or split.
- handoff_event: When request ownership moves between worker threads or nodes.
- resource_pressure: Node-level signals (gpu_memory_pct, active_streams, nvlink_health).

Event schema examples (JSON):
1) scheduler_decision sample:
{
  "event_type": "scheduler_decision",
  "request_id": "req-20260223-7c9b2",
  "tenant_id": "team-optimizer",
  "priority": "P0",
  "decision": "accept",
  "reason": "admitted_to_slot",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-23T17:12:03.123Z"
}

2) batch_formation sample:
{
  "event_type": "batch_formation",
  "batch_id": "b-4491",
  "shape": "[1,8,64]",
  "kernel_hint": "attention_v2_fp16",
  "requests": ["req-7c9b2", "req-8a1d0"],
  "queued_ms": 12,
  "timestamp": "2026-02-23T17:12:03.135Z"
}

Metric table (concrete list for dashboards and alerts):
| metric_name | unit | description | floor_sampling | alert_threshold | owner |
| scheduler.admit_rate | requests/s | Rate of accepted requests post-admission | unsampled for P0/P1 | sustained < 5th percentile baseline for 5m | runtime-sre |
| scheduler.queue_latency_p95 | ms | 95th percentile time between enqueue and batch dispatch | 100% for P0 traces | > 200 ms increase vs baseline | runtime-sre |
| scheduler.batch_size.avg | requests | Rolling average batch size per kernel | sampled 10% | step-change > 30% | runtime |
| scheduler.preempt_rate | events/s | Number of preemption events | unsampled for P0 | > expected floor for 10m | runtime |
| node.resource_pressure | pct | Node-level memory utilization | sampled 5% | > 90% for 3m | infra |

Sampling rules and guarantees:
- P0 (latency-critical) requests: all scheduler_decision and batch_formation events must be emitted unsampled and preserved for 72 hours.
- P1: floor sampling 10% for high-volume events; core transition events unsampled.
- Node-level telemetry: aggregated at 1s resolution, retained 14 days.
- If budget / ingestion pressure is detected, the horizon for batch_size.avg and resource_pressure can be downsampled but scheduler_decision for P0 must remain.

Trace and span conventions:
- Each request carries a trace_id and request_id in all emitted events. Spans are tagged with: service=scheduler, kernel=..., slot_id=..., tenant_id=...
- Parent-child relationships: scheduler_decision -> batch_formation -> kernel_dispatch -> kernel_execution_span (if available).

Simulated Injector (overview):
The Simulated Injector (sim-injector) is a lightweight binary and set of test harness scripts that synthesizes scheduler events and metrics to validate the entire telemetry ingestion, enrichment, and alerting pipeline. The injector supports:
- Normal steady-state profiles (latency-sensitive and throughput-oriented shapes)
- Pathological cases (burst admission storms, opaque kernel failures, preemption cascades)
- Configurable tenant-mix, sequence-length distributions, and kernel-hint compositions

Key features:
- Deterministic replay mode: replays a seed corpus to reproduce prior incidents.
- Fuzz mode: randomizes batch shapes and decision jitter to stress sampling invariants.
- Backpressure faucet: emits resource_pressure events under operator control to exercise degradation paths.

How to run (local quickstart):
Prereqs: go 1.20+ or prebuilt binary; access to dev telemetry ingestion endpoint (env var TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT).

1) Build or fetch binary:
$ go build ./cmd/sim-injector -o sim-injector

2) Run a simple steady-state profile (10 tenants, 100 rps):
$ TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT=https://dev-telemetry.redwood.internal:443 
  ./sim-injector --profile steady --tenants 10 --rps 100 --duration 300s

3) Run a preemption cascade scenario and persist traces to local file for debugging:
$ ./sim-injector --scenario preempt-cascade --out-file preempt-trace.json --duration 120s

4) Replay a saved trace against staging ingestion to validate alerting rules:
$ ./sim-injector --replay preempt-trace.json --target staging

Acceptance tests (gating a scheduler change):
- Unit: New decision code emits scheduler_decision with new field kernel_version (if added) and passes JSON schema validation.
- Integration: Run sim-injector steady profile at 10% of production RPS for 30m into staging; no increase in queue_latency_p95 > 10% and no unhandled preemptions.
- Observability smoke: All P0 traces appear in the P95 latency dashboard and sample logs link back to request_id.

Rollout checklist for scheduler changes that affect the contract:
1) Update this document and add schema diff (PR).
2) Coordinate with telemetry owners and alerting oncall.
3) Add compatibility shim to runtime that emits legacy fields for 14 days.
4) Run sim-injector compatibility runs against staging ingestion and dashboards.
5) Canary deploy scheduler change to 1% traffic with active sim-injector shadowing.
6) Verify metrics and tracing invariants for 24h, then expand canary.

Ownership and escalation:
- Scheduler telemetry contract owner: Priya Raman (runtime observability).
- Ingestion and enrichment: Observability Platform (owner: Ethan Cole).
- Oncall escalation: runtime-sre rotation (page: #runtime-sre).
- For schema changes: require review by Observability Platform and Runtime leads.

Appendix A — JSON Schema (abridged):
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["event_type", "timestamp", "request_id"],
  "properties": {
    "event_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["scheduler_decision", "batch_formation", "kernel_dispatch", "preemption_event", "handoff_event", "resource_pressure"]
    },
    "timestamp": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time"
    },
    "request_id": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
}

Appendix B — Common troubleshooting scenarios and quick checks:
- Missing P0 events in dashboards: verify tracer injection, check trace sampling policy, confirm TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT and auth tokens, and run sim-injector --replay for a P0 trace.
- High preempt_rate after change: run sim-injector preempt-cascade and compare kernel_dispatch vs preemption_event counts.
- Alert noise due to downsampling: confirm sampling floor is honored for P0; if not, escalate to Observability Platform.

If you modify any event names or fields, update the schema in Appendix A, notify reviewers listed above, and run the sim-injector compatibility suite before merging.
